Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
11.3 Suspected Violations

IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:

b. remove or require removal of any offending Content;

Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Customer will promptly notify IBM of any event or circumstance related to this Agreement, Customer's use of the Services, or Content of which Customer becomes aware that could lead to a claim or demand against IBM, and Customer will provide all relevant information relating to such event or circumstance to IBM at IBM's request.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

paragraphs.text: 4.2 Payment

IBM invoices will specify the amount due. Payment is due upon receipt and payable as specified in such invoice. Customer agrees to pay accordingly, including any late payment fees. Payment will be made in United States dollars.
4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Category: audit

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 9.2 Customer's Limitation of Liability

Circumstances may arise where, because of a default on Customer's part or other liability, IBM is entitled to recover damages from Customer. Regardless of the basis on which IBM is entitled to claim damages from Customer (including fundamental breach, negligence, misrepresentation, or other contract or tort claim), Customer is liable for no more than:
a. Indemnification payments as provided in Section 8.2;
b. damages for bodily injury (including death) and damage to real property and tangible personal property; and

(c) the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services. The foregoing limit also applies to any of Customer's Affiliates. It is the cumulative maximum for which Customer and its Affiliates are collectively responsible. Under no circumstances is Customer or its Affiliates liable for any third party claims against IBM for damages (other than those

Kind: direction

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

Category: licence

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 14.10 Assignment (p0188)**

- **Issue:** The assignment restriction runs one way only. Customer needs IBM's consent to assign; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a Customer competitor. Customer's carve-out covers only "merger, consolidation or acquisition" — no affiliate transfers, no sale of substantially all assets, and it is not clearly consent-free.
- **Change-of-control check:** No "change of control" language anywhere in the agreement; § 3.3 termination is breach-only, so IBM has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. No deletion needed.
- **Redline (validated, preferred):** Customer may assign without IBM's consent to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; IBM may not assign without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor. Fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice) offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 14.10 restricts only Customer assignment. The M&A carve-out is partial: it omits assignment to affiliates and to a purchaser of substantially all assets, and it is unclear whether the carve-out dispenses with IBM's consent. The clause imposes no reciprocal restriction on IBM, so IBM could freely assign, including to a Customer competitor. No change-of-control termination right exists for IBM (§3.3 is breach-only), so no deletion is needed there. Redline adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out without consent and a reciprocal, reasonableness-qualified consent requirement on IBM with a competitor prohibition; fallback of mutual successor assignment on notice offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement without IBM's consent to an affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. IBM will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Customer. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added our customary right to assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made the consent restriction reciprocal so IBM cannot assign to a Customer competitor. If helpful, we can accept a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice, with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM could withdraw use rights at will, and it runs to "Customer" only — Affiliates (a defined term in the preamble) and contractors operating the Services on our behalf are not covered, and § 14.17 confirms no rights beyond those expressly granted. Successor transfer is already protected by § 14.10 (assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition), so the minimal edit adds affiliate/contractor scope and ties revocation to expiration or termination under Section 3.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM could withdraw use rights at will, and it runs to "Customer" only — Affiliates (a defined term in the preamble) and contractors operating the Services on our behalf are not covered, and § 14.17 confirms no rights beyond those expressly granted. Successor transfer is already protected by § 14.10 (assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition), so the minimal edit adds affiliate/contractor scope and ties revocation to expiration or termination under Section 3.

Title: Vendor insurance

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence to include modification, and confirm Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components.
input.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so Materials created during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned) rather than IBM-owned, and the licence to IBM's pre-existing Type II Materials embedded in deliverables should let us modify them for our business. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high) — § 12.1 License**

The grant fails the LICENSE rule on two of three parameters:

- **Revocable at will.** "nonexclusive, **revocable** license" with no standard or trigger — IBM could withdraw our right to use the Base Components unilaterally, even while we continue paying for Services.
- **Affiliates and contractors excluded.** The grant runs to "Customer" only, and § 14.17 (Limitation of Licenses) forecloses any implied extension. Our Affiliates are a defined term (preamble ¶ b) and are used elsewhere (§ 9.2), so scoping them in is consistent with the rest of the bargain. § 14.11 (no resale) remains intact, so this is internal-use scope only, not resale.
- **Successor transfer — already satisfied.** § 14.10 permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so no edit was needed there.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** extend the grant to "Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf," delete "revocable," and tie any revocation to expiration or termination under Section 3.

Fallback offered in the comment: affiliate coverage on written notice, if IBM resists automatic extension.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM could withdraw use rights at will, and it runs to "Customer" only — Affiliates (a defined term in the preamble) and contractors operating the Services on our behalf are not covered, and § 14.17 confirms no rights beyond those expressly granted. Successor transfer is already protected by § 14.10 (assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition), so the minimal edit adds affiliate/contractor scope and ties revocation to expiration or termination under Section 3.

Original paragraphs:
p0149: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0149: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Such license is irrevocable during the term of the applicable Services and may be terminated only upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or the applicable Service Option Attachment in accordance with Section 3. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to contractors using the Services on our behalf, and removed "revocable" so the licence cannot be pulled at will — it should end only when this Agreement or the relevant Services terminate. If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice as a fallback.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 defaults all delivered Materials to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third-party) owned, with the Customer receiving only an internal-Enterprise licence and no right to modify. That reverses our position that we own deliverables created for us, with IBM retaining only pre-existing IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is only addressed as our responsibility at 11.6, and 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). Redline flips the default to Type I, extends the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and adds an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence to include modification, and confirm Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so Materials created during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned) rather than IBM-owned, and the licence to IBM's pre-existing Type II Materials embedded in deliverables should let us modify them for our business. We have also added a confirmation that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components, with no assignment or joint ownership; if IBM cannot move the default, our fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Materials for our business.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 defaults all delivered Materials to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third-party) owned, with the Customer receiving only an internal-Enterprise licence and no right to modify. That reverses our position that we own deliverables created for us, with IBM retaining only pre-existing IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is only addressed as our responsibility at 11.6, and 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). Redline flips the default to Type I, extends the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and adds an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) requires Customer to pay uncapped "early termination charges" set out in Attachment A/Service Option Attachments as a condition of terminating for convenience — a Customer-payable liquidated amount of unknown size, with no stated ceiling (and Section 10 further preserves IBM's ability to claim amounts for Services "that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach"). Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; because the convenience-termination right is the counterweight to this charge, we applied the accepted fallback and capped the charge at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on such termination. No service credits or Vendor-payable LDs are affected.

input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) requires Customer to pay uncapped "early termination charges" set out in Attachment A/Service Option Attachments as a condition of terminating for convenience — a Customer-payable liquidated amount of unknown size, with no stated ceiling (and Section 10 further preserves IBM's ability to claim amounts for Services "that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach"). Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; because the convenience-termination right is the counterweight to this charge, we applied the accepted fallback and capped the charge at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on such termination. No service credits or Vendor-payable LDs are affected.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.rationale: § 5.1 contains only a "reasonable care and skill" services standard (broadly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) plus authority and a narrow law-compliance covenant. There is no warranty that Materials/deliverables conform to documentation, no malicious code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy anywhere in the agreement (searches for "conform", "malicious" and "remedy" return nothing relevant). Worse, § 5.4(c) provides all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out, so the disclaimer swallows any deliverable-level protection — close to the walk-away position. Redline adds a 90-day conformance warranty, a malicious code warranty and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and carves the § 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical, ip-data).**

What I found in the IBM e-business Hosting Agreement:

- **§ 7(a) (p0082)** — all Materials delivered to us default to **Type II**, i.e. owned by IBM or third parties, unless the parties expressly agree otherwise. That means work product created for us during the Service performance period lands in IBM's hands by default, contrary to our position that we own what we pay for.
- **§ 7(c) (p0085)** — the Type II licence back to us is irrevocable/worldwide/paid-up but limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" with **no right to modify or prepare derivative works**, which falls short of even our fallback position.
- **No Customer Data / Content ownership statement anywhere.** Content and Customer Components are defined (p0017, p0019) and § 11.6 only makes us *responsible* for Content; § 14.17 confirms no rights arise beyond those expressly granted, so there is no affirmative confirmation that we retain title.
- Nothing assigns our IP or data to IBM and there is no joint ownership, so no walk-away trigger. IBM's ownership of the Base Components (§ 12.1) is acceptable.

Redline (validated ok:true): flip the § 7 default to **Type I** (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence to be perpetual and to permit derivative works and use for the operation of our business, and add a new § 7(e) confirming we retain all right, title and interest in Content and Customer Components with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership. Fallback offered in the comment if IBM will not move the default.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7 defaults all delivered Materials to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third-party) owned, with the Customer receiving only an internal-Enterprise licence and no right to modify. That reverses our position that we own deliverables created for us, with IBM retaining only pre-existing IP under a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back. The Agreement also nowhere confirms that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is only addressed as our responsibility at 11.6, and 14.17 grants no rights beyond those expressly stated). Redline flips the default to Type I, extends the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and adds an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute, and prepare derivative works based on copies of Type II Materials, within Customer's Enterprise and for the operation of Customer's business.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.
e. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers any such rights to IBM or creates any joint ownership of them.

Comment:
[Playbook] We own what we pay for, so Materials created during the Services should default to Type I (Customer-owned) rather than IBM-owned, and the licence to IBM's pre-existing Type II Materials embedded in deliverables should let us modify them for our business. We have also added a confirmation that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components, with no assignment or joint ownership; if IBM cannot move the default, our fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Materials for our business.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale: Section 11.3 is the only audit/inspection-type right binding Customer: IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty at will. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

input.rationale: Section 11.3 is the only audit/inspection-type right binding Customer: IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty at will. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 3.4(b), Termination for Convenience**

- **Issue:** Our convenience-termination right is conditioned on "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — an open-ended, Customer-payable liquidated amount fixed outside the negotiated body of the agreement, with no ceiling. Section 10 compounds the exposure by preserving IBM's claim for amounts owing for Services "that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach."
- **Direction check:** No service credits or IBM-payable liquidated damages exist here that would be affected; Section 3.3 only removes the charge where IBM is in breach, which does not cure the convenience case.
- **Redline (validated, fallback level, per precedent seed-ld):** cap the charge at three months' recurring charges for the terminated Services and make it the sole payment obligation and IBM's sole remedy for that termination. Preferred deletion was disproportionate given the charge is the counterweight to our one-month convenience right.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4(b) requires Customer to pay uncapped "early termination charges" set out in Attachment A/Service Option Attachments as a condition of terminating for convenience — a Customer-payable liquidated amount of unknown size, with no stated ceiling (and Section 10 further preserves IBM's ability to claim amounts for Services "that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach"). Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; because the convenience-termination right is the counterweight to this charge, we applied the accepted fallback and capped the charge at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on such termination. No service credits or Vendor-payable LDs are affected.

Original paragraphs:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0123: a. In no event will either party be liable to the other for special, incidental, or indirect damages or for any consequential damages (including lost profits or savings), even if they are informed of the possibility; provided that this Section 10 does not apply to Customer's failure to pay any amounts owing to IBM under this Agreement (including amounts owing for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach of this Agreement).

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring charges for the terminated Services and will be Customer's sole payment obligation and IBM's sole remedy arising from such termination.

Comment:
[Playbook] Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us, so we have capped the open-ended early termination charges at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on a convenience termination. This keeps our termination right meaningful while accepting the accepted fallback cap rather than deleting the charge entirely.

paragraphs.text: 4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
11.5 Capacity Planning

Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.
3.1 Term

This Agreement will be effective beginning on 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on the day after the date of last signature to these Base Terms ("Effective Date") and ending on the expiration and/or termination of all Service Option Attachments, unless the Agreement is terminated earlier in accordance with the terms herein. The term of each Service Option Attachment is as specified on the applicable Order Form.
3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.

**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, WARRANTY).**

What I found:
- **§ 5.1** gives a services performance standard ("reasonable care and skill... degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession") plus corporate authority and a narrow covenant to comply with "laws applicable to IBM's business." That part is broadly acceptable.

Document-wide searches for "conform", "malicious" and "remedy" returned nothing on point; §§ 11.1 and 12.2 impose Customer support duties and IBM-discretion maintenance only, so they don't supply a warranty remedy.

Rule:

Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 5.1 contains only a "reasonable care and skill" services standard (broadly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) plus authority and a narrow law-compliance covenant. There is no warranty that Materials/deliverables conform to documentation, no malicious code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy anywhere in the agreement (searches for "conform", "malicious" and "remedy" return nothing relevant). Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 11.3 is the only audit/inspection-type right binding Customer: IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty at will. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

Original paragraphs:
p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.
p0138: Customer will promptly notify IBM of any event or circumstance related to this Agreement, Customer's use of the Services, or Content of which Customer becomes aware that could lead to a claim or demand against IBM, and Customer will provide all relevant information relating to such event or circumstance to IBM at IBM's request.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE)**

**What I found.** The Agreement contains no insurance provision at all — a full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the section outline has no insurance heading anywhere in the miscellaneous article (§ 14) or elsewhere.

**Why it matters here.** IBM is squarely a data-touching hosting vendor:
- § 5.3 (Security) confirms IBM operates the e-business Hosting Environment and implements security features for it.
- § 14.12 (Risk of Loss) shows IBM holds Base Components, with Customer Components in its environment.
- § 14.18 (Data Protection) states IBM processes **personal information on Customer's behalf** as part of the Services.

That last point puts the gap at the playbook's walk-away line ("no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data"), so this is not a waivable omission despite the rule's low severity.

**Redline.** Inserted a new § 14.12A "Insurance" immediately after the existing ri[REDACTED] paragraph — the most natural anchor, since it sits with the other risk provisions and avoids renumbering §§ 14.13–14.20. Coverage is at the preferred level: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M (justified by the § 14.18 personal-data processing), statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, running through the term plus one year. Validated via `propose_redline` (ok:true) and aligned to the `seed-insurance` precedent.

**Negotiation note.** The comment flags the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) up front. Practically, IBM carries coverage well in excess of these limits, so the likely friction is procedural — IBM often resists contractual certificate-delivery obligations and prefers pointing to its corporate insurance program rather than accepting per-contract limits. If they push back, the certificates-on-request sentence is the cheaper concession to trade than the cyber limit.

Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and the section outline contains no insurance provision, so the Agreement is silent on vendor coverage. IBM is a hosting vendor that operates the e-business Hosting Environment and holds Customer Components (§ 14.12) and processes personal information on Customer's behalf (§ 14.18), which triggers the playbook's cyber/privacy requirement and makes the walk-away position (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data) applicable. We inserted a short insurance covenant as new § 14.12A, adjacent to the existing ri[REDACTED] provision in the miscellaneous article, at the preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback offered in the comment.

Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.

IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

Comment:
[Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision, so we added our standard coverage requirements (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, and cyber USD 5M since IBM hosts and processes Customer Data and personal data on our behalf under §§ 5.3 and 14.18), plus certificates on request. The redline implements the accepted fallback verbatim in substance — an aggregate cap of three months' recurring charges, expressed as the sole amount/remedy arising from the convenience termination — and is scoped to termination-related amounts so it does not disturb accrued fees for Services actually rendered.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is an artifact of a very short source sentence; the change is an appended proviso only, with no deletion or rewording of the original obligation, which is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.
