paragraphs.text: 14.18 Data Protection

You agree to allow International Business Machines Corporation and entities within its Enterprise to store and use your contact information, including names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses, anywhere they do business. Such information will be processed and used in connection with our business relationship, and may be provided to contractors, Business Partners, and assignees of IBM Corp. and entities within its Enterprise for uses consistent with their collective business activities, including communicating with you (for example, for processing orders, for promotions, and for marketing research). For personal information processed by IBM on your behalf as part of the Services, IBM will act in accordance with your instructions by following such processing and security obligations as are contained in this Agreement. You also confirm that you are solely responsible for ensuring that any processing and security obligations comply with applicable data protection laws. Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf.
14.2 Survival

Any of these terms and conditions which by their nature extend beyond the Agreement termination or expiration remain in effect until fulfilled, including, without limitation, Sections 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.2, 11.3, 11.6, 12.2, 12.3, and 14, and apply to both Customer's and IBM's respective successors and assignees.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic appears anywhere in the Base Terms: searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return nothing on point. Under § 4.1 Charges are only for Services ordered under Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. fees for usage or ordered services only, which matches our preferred position. § 11.5 Capacity Planning imposes no usage floor or cap on Customer — it merely allocates responsibility to Customer for sizing and requesting capacity changes. Customer also retains an exit under § 3.4, terminating the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience at month end on one month's notice, subject only to early termination charges "if any" specified in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments (not part of this document). No redline required; we would review Attachment A and each Order Form for any committed volumes or early termination charges before signature.

Original paragraphs:
p0052: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0142: Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Order Forms: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0052: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0142: Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

Comment:
none

reasons: Deviation is correctly characterized: § 5.1 gives only a reasonable-care services standard plus authority/law-compliance, with no documentation-conformance warranty, no malicious code warranty and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy, while p0074 puts all Materials 'AS IS' with no express-warranty carve-out — materially below the playbook position and close to walk-away.

Redline is actionable and reaches the rule's model language: adds a 90-day conformance warranty on Deliverables/Materials, a malicious code warranty, and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and inserts 'EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1' into the disclaimer so it no longer swallows the express warranty.

The failed 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' check is a regex false negative: the inserted text reads 'for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery', which satisfies the rule (and matches the rule's own model language and fallback for services/deliverables).
The 0.460 changed-character ratio on p0074 reflects only a short prefixed carve-out on an otherwise untouched all-caps disclaimer; that is the smallest edit that achieves the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites §§ 5.1 and 5.4(c), states what changed and why, and offers a shorter-period fallback in the required tone.

Minor drafting nits only (not fatal): p0062's terminal period was not converted to '; and' before the new items (c)/(d), and the remedy sentence is appended inside item (d) rather than standing alone; the 'knowingly ... introduced by IBM' qualifier also slightly weakens the malicious code warranty relative to the preferred position and could be tightened in negotiation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 11.6 Content and Digital Certificates
Customer is solely responsible for:
a. all Content including, without limitation, its selection, licensing, accuracy, performance, maintenance, and support; and
b. the selection, management and use of any public and private keys and digital certificates it may use with the Services.
3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

reasons: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.

Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.

Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.

The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.

Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT), confidence 0.72.**

- **Where:** § 11.3 "Suspected Violations" (p0132, p0137, p0138). The agreement contains no clause using the word "audit"; the only inspection-type right binding us is IBM's reservation of "the right to investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b), backed by our obligation in p0138 to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request.
- **Why it deviates:** No frequency cap, no advance notice (p0137's notice is only a best-efforts attempt before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours limit, no independent-auditor/confidentiality requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to our systems. Unlimited/unannounced audits fall at the playbook walk-away line.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a single proviso after p0137 imposing the preferred position — one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, IBM or an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM bearing all costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct or remote access to our systems, with off-site information delivery permitted. IBM's substantive remedies in 11.3(a)–(d) are untouched, and the comment flags the 15-day/10% fallback.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.; Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.; Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.; The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.; Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits on IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale: Section 11.3 is the only audit/inspection-type right binding Customer: IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty at will. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT), confidence 0.72.**

- **Where:** § 11.3 "Suspected Violations" (p0132, p0137, p0138). The agreement contains no clause using the word "audit"; the only inspection-type right binding us is IBM's reservation of "the right to investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b), backed by our obligation in p0138 to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request.
- **Why it deviates:** No frequency cap, no advance notice (p0137's notice is only a best-efforts attempt before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours limit, no independent-auditor/confidentiality requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to our systems. Unlimited/unannounced audits fall at the playbook walk-away line.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a single proviso after p0137 imposing the preferred position — one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, IBM or an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM bearing all costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct or remote access to our systems, with off-site information delivery permitted. IBM's substantive remedies in 11.3(a)–(d) are untouched, and the comment flags the 15-day/10% fallback.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.; Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.; Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.; The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.; Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.

input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT), confidence 0.72.**

- **Where:** § 11.3 "Suspected Violations" (p0132, p0137, p0138). The agreement contains no clause using the word "audit"; the only inspection-type right binding us is IBM's reservation of "the right to investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b), backed by our obligation in p0138 to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request.
- **Why it deviates:** No frequency cap, no advance notice (p0137's notice is only a best-efforts attempt before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours limit, no independent-auditor/confidentiality requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to our systems. Unlimited/unannounced audits fall at the playbook walk-away line.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a single proviso after p0137 imposing the preferred position — one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, IBM or an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM bearing all costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct or remote access to our systems, with off-site information delivery permitted. IBM's substantive remedies in 11.3(a)–(d) are untouched, and the comment flags the 15-day/10% fallback.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.; Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.; Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.; The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.; Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.
Repair the finding, validate it again, and submit it.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: On review, the AUDIT rule has no target in this agreement. There is no usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit right binding Customer: no clause uses audit, inspect, verify, examine or records-access language against us; § 4.1/4.2 have IBM meter and invoice its own usage Charges without any right to audit our books; and § 12.1 grants a licence with no compliance-verification right. The only inspection-flavoured provision, § 11.3, is an abuse/acceptable-use enforcement right — IBM investigating suspected breaches of the content/AUP warranties in § 11.2(b) — which is a security and illegal-content mechanism, not a commercial audit, and § 11.3(a)/(b) plus p0137's emergency carve-out are the counterparts to that. Grafting audit-style limits (annual cap, 30 days' notice, 5% underpayment cost-shift, blanket no-systems-access) onto it would be directionally wrong in a hosting deal where IBM operates the environment: it would contradict p0137's emergency/legal-requirement notice standard and p0138's information obligation, bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident, and import an inoperative payment trigger where no quantity is measured. I therefore withdraw the earlier insertion. The absence of any audit right against Customer is better than the playbook preferred position and favours us, so no redline is warranted; if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification, the AUDIT parameters should be applied there.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Verifier feedback: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.; Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.; Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.; The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.; Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.

content.text:
**Finding: Missing (medium severity) — TRANSITION**

The agreement has no post-termination transition or data return mechanism:

- **§ 3.5 (Effect of Termination)** is a single paragraph dealing only with Customer's accrued payment obligations and continuing charges under other Service Option Attachments.
- Searches for "transition", "delete", and "return" turn up nothing relevant — the only "return" hits are the IP indemnity (§ 8.1, requiring *us* to return Materials) and the signature block.
- **§ 14.18 (Data Protection)** covers only contact information processing, not return or deletion of our data.
- **§ 11.6** makes Customer solely responsible for all Content but gives no corresponding retrieval right.

This is materially adverse in a hosting deal where all of our Content sits in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment — on termination we would have no contractual right to get it back, and no deletion assurance.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** inserted a new paragraph after p0049 in § 3.5 giving (a) up to six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates on request, (b) return/retrieval of all Content in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and (c) certified deletion thereafter. I anchored it in § 3.5 deliberately: § 14.2 (Survival) already lists Section 3.5, so the new obligations survive termination without any further amendment.

The comment flags our fallback (90 days of assistance, same 30-day export window) in case IBM pushes back on the six-month tail.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.comment: [Playbook] We added standard limits to IBM's investigation right: no more than one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless an underpayment over 5% is found, and no access to our systems. As drafted the right is unlimited and unannounced, which our playbook treats as a walk-away; we can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold as a fallback.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. No such investigation will include direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records, and Customer may satisfy any such investigation by providing relevant information off-site.

There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. Unlimited and unannounced audits are the playbook walk-away, so we inserted the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access) as a single proviso in § 11.3, leaving IBM's substantive remedies untouched.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT), confidence 0.72.**

- **Where:** § 11.3 "Suspected Violations" (p0132, p0137, p0138). The agreement contains no clause using the word "audit"; the only inspection-type right binding us is IBM's reservation of "the right to investigate potential violations" of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b), backed by our obligation in p0138 to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request.
- **Why it deviates:** No frequency cap, no advance notice (p0137's notice is only a best-efforts attempt before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours limit, no independent-auditor/confidentiality requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to our systems. Unlimited/unannounced audits fall at the playbook walk-away line.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a single proviso after p0137 imposing the preferred position — one investigation per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, our normal business hours, IBM or an independent auditor bound by the AECI, IBM bearing all costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct or remote access to our systems, with off-site information delivery permitted. IBM's substantive remedies in 11.3(a)–(d) are untouched, and the comment flags the 15-day/10% fallback.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: Rule mis-applied: § 11.3 is an abuse/AUP enforcement right (IBM investigating potential breaches of the Customer's content/acceptable-use warranties in 11.2(b)), not a usage/licence-compliance or metering audit of the kind AUDIT targets. Burdening a security/illegal-content investigation right with audit-style limits is directionally wrong; if the contract truly lacks a usage-audit clause, the correct output is a 'missing/no-issue' finding, not this graft.; Internal inconsistency created in the edited paragraph: p0137 expressly preserves IBM's ability to act 'in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law' with only best-efforts notice, but the inserted proviso imposes an absolute 30 days' prior written notice and a once-per-12-month cap on 'any investigation' with no emergency carve-out — the two sentences now contradict each other and the once-a-year cap would bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident.; Cost-shift trigger is inapposite: there is no payment/quantity measurement in § 11.3, so 'unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated' is inoperative boilerplate transplanted from a licence-audit context and will read as a drafting error to the counterparty.; The blanket bar on 'direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, facilities or records' and the off-site-satisfaction right sit awkwardly in a hosting agreement where IBM operates the environment and § 11.3(a)/(b) contemplate restricting access to or removing Content; as drafted it arguably neuters the remedies the rationale claims were left untouched, and it conflicts with p0138's obligation to provide all relevant information on request.; Comment overstates the baseline ('unlimited and unannounced ... walk-away') given p0137's existing best-efforts notice obligation, so the justification offered to the counterparty is not fully accurate.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: On review, the AUDIT rule has no target in this agreement. There is no usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit right binding Customer: no clause uses audit, inspect, verify, examine or records-access language against us; § 4.1/4.2 have IBM meter and invoice its own usage Charges without any right to audit our books; and § 12.1 grants a licence with no compliance-verification right. The only inspection-flavoured provision, § 11.3, is an abuse/acceptable-use enforcement right — IBM investigating suspected breaches of the content/AUP warranties in § 11.2(b) — which is a security and illegal-content mechanism, not a commercial audit, and § 11.3(a)/(b) plus p0137's emergency carve-out are the counterparts to that. Grafting audit-style limits (annual cap, 30 days' notice, 5% underpayment cost-shift, blanket no-systems-access) onto it would be directionally wrong in a hosting deal where IBM operates the environment: it would contradict p0137's emergency/legal-requirement notice standard and p0138's information obligation, bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident, and import an inoperative payment trigger where no quantity is measured. I therefore withdraw the earlier insertion. The absence of any audit right against Customer is better than the playbook preferred position and favours us, so no redline is warranted; if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification, the AUDIT parameters should be applied there.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of the AECI. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation, including the costs of any auditor, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period investigated. There is no frequency cap, no advance notice requirement (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt before restricting access or removing Content, not before an investigation), no business-hours or independent-auditor requirement, no cost allocation, and no bar on access to Customer systems — while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over "all relevant information" on IBM's request. input.rationale: On review, the AUDIT rule has no target in this agreement. There is no usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit right binding Customer: no clause uses audit, inspect, verify, examine or records-access language against us; § 4.1/4.2 have IBM meter and invoice its own usage Charges without any right to audit our books; and § 12.1 grants a licence with no compliance-verification right. The only inspection-flavoured provision, § 11.3, is an abuse/acceptable-use enforcement right — IBM investigating suspected breaches of the content/AUP warranties in § 11.2(b) — which is a security and illegal-content mechanism, not a commercial audit, and § 11.3(a)/(b) plus p0137's emergency carve-out are the counterparts to that. Grafting audit-style limits (annual cap, 30 days' notice, 5% underpayment cost-shift, blanket no-systems-access) onto it would be directionally wrong in a hosting deal where IBM operates the environment: it would contradict p0137's emergency/legal-requirement notice standard and p0138's information obligation, bar IBM from responding to a second abuse or security incident, and import an inoperative payment trigger where no quantity is measured. I therefore withdraw the earlier insertion. The absence of any audit right against Customer is better than the playbook preferred position and favours us, so no redline is warranted; if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification, the AUDIT parameters should be applied there.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement (document excerpt reviewed: 3.1 Term and Base Terms) 
**Status:** 18 findings verified — 3 critical, 5 high, 9 medium, 1 low

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in IBM's favour in three areas that we regard as must-fix before signature:

- **Liability (§ 9.1).** The cap is mutual at 12 months' charges, but the floor is $100,000 (against our $1,000,000 preferred position), is measured on charges *paid* only, there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and § 9.1(2) **wholly excludes IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data** — which guts our remedy in a hosting deal.
- **Indemnities (§ 8.1 / § 8.2).** IBM's indemnity is IP-only (meeting our fallback for IP), with no cover for IBM's breach of law, IBM-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, or IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Meanwhile our reverse indemnity at § 8.2(a)(3) covers any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — effectively a one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services. This is a walk-away item.
- **IP ownership (§ 7 / § 5.4).** All delivered Materials default to Type II (IBM-owned), giving us only an internal-Enterprise licence with no right to modify, and nothing in the Agreement confirms we retain rights in our Content and Customer Components.

Beyond these, our exit economics are unquantified: convenience termination under § 3.4 is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges with no ceiling and no refund of prepaid charges, there is **no transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation anywhere** in the Agreement, and there is **no vendor insurance provision at all** despite IBM operating the hosting environment and processing personal information. Warranty protection is thin (reasonable care and skill only, with Materials supplied "AS IS" under § 5.4(c)).

On the positive side, four playbook risks are simply absent and we should preserve that: no exclusivity or non-compete on us (§ 14.16 Freedom of Action expressly preserves both parties' freedom to contract with others), no MFN burden, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (§ 4.1), no audit right against us, and no non-solicitation restriction on us (§ 14.8). Governing law is already New York, our preferred choice; only the forum element is missing.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | IBM indemnity is IP-only; missing breach of law, IBM-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct heads. Our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is far broader than the playbook allows. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with § 7) | Materials default to Type II (IBM-owned), internal-Enterprise licence only, no modification right; no confirmation that we retain rights in Content and Customer Components. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Floor $100,000 on charges "paid" only; no Excluded Claims carve-outs; § 9.1(2) excludes all IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restricts only our assignment; M&A carve-out omits affiliates and asset sales and is unclear on consent; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a competitor. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Uncapped early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A / Service Option Attachments, with no stated ceiling; § 10 also preserves IBM's claim for Services that would have been rendered but for our breach. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" with no standard and runs to Customer only — Affiliates and contractors operating the Services for us are not covered (§ 14.17 grants nothing further). |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No sole-supply or exclusive-dealing obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. No redline. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Compliant** | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant on us; only restrictions are the § 14.11 resale bar and licence-scope limits. No redline. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law is our preferred position, but there is no venue or forum clause and no arbitration provision; exclusive New York County jurisdiction is missing. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term (so multi-year renewals where an Order Form sets a multi-year initial term) on 90 days' non-renewal notice; renewal uplift uncapped. |
| 11 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | We have a ~30-day convenience right and IBM has none (good), but the right is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges and there is no refund of prepaid charges (§ 3.5 only accelerates our payment obligations). |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition assistance, Content return/export or deletion-certification obligation anywhere; § 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations. All our data sits in IBM's hosting environment. |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Reasonable care and skill only; no conformance-to-documentation or malicious code warranty and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. § 5.4(c) supplies all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification: fail) | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No usage, metering or licence-compliance audit right exists against us; § 11.3 is an abuse/acceptable-use investigation right. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is an artefact of there being no audit clause to parameterise. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | **Compliant** | § 4.1 Charges | No terms- or pricing-parity obligation on us. Absence of a vendor-granted MFN in our favour is a commercial upside item, not a playbook deviation. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Compliant** | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic; charges apply only to Services ordered. § 11.5 Capacity Planning imposes no usage floor or cap. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification: fail) | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on us; § 14.8 covers only each party's own personnel and IBM's subcontracting. Failed duration and general-solicitation sub-checks are non-probative because there is no restriction to parameterise. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | Agreement is silent on insurance, yet IBM operates the hosting environment, holds Customer Components (§ 14.12) and processes personal information on our behalf (§ 14.18). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not sign as drafted:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services.** Indemnifying IBM against any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is expressly a walk-away item under the playbook, only partly mitigated by the relief in § 8.2(c). We require this narrowed to our breach of law or of this Agreement.
2. **§ 9.1(2) — blanket exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data.** In a hosting deal this removes our principal remedy and must be deleted; it also needs to be read with the absence of any data-breach indemnity in § 8.1.
3. **§ 5.4(c) — all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out.** Combined with the absence of any conformance, malicious code or remedy provision, this sits close to the walk-away position on warranties. At minimum the § 5.1 warranties must be carved out of the disclaimer.
4. **No vendor insurance where IBM processes personal data.** The playbook treats a vendor processing personal data with no insurance as a walk-away; we require the covenant at § 14.12A.
5. **§ 3.2 — automatic multi-year renewals.** Where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term, § 3.2 produces automatic multi-year renewals, which is at the walk-away boundary. Renewal terms must be fixed at 12 months.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Redlines issued (critical and high):**
1. § 8.1 — add IBM indemnity heads for breach of applicable law, IBM-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, placed inside § 8.1 so they benefit from the uncapped treatment in § 9.1(a) and the existing notice/control/cooperation procedure; narrow our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity to our breach of law or of this Agreement.
2. § 9.1 — raise the mutual floor to $1,000,000 on fees **paid or payable**, add a mutual Excluded Claims provision (confidentiality/data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and delete the § 9.1(2) data-loss exclusion. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion in § 10, with its carve-out for our payment obligations, is acceptable as drafted.
3. § 7 / § 5.4 — flip the default to Type I (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and add an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement for Content and Customer Components.
4. § 14.10 — add an affiliate and substantially-all-assets carve-out for our assignment without IBM consent, plus a reciprocal reasonableness-qualified consent requirement on IBM with a competitor prohibition. **Fallback offered:** mutual successor assignment on notice. No change to § 3.3, which is breach-only.
5. § 3.4 — delete the uncapped early termination charge and add a 30-day pro-rata refund of prepaid charges. **Fallback offered:** cap the charge at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on convenience termination.
6. § 12.1 — extend the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and contractors operating the Services on our behalf, and tie revocation to expiration or termination under § 3 rather than IBM's discretion.

**Redlines issued (medium and low):**
7. § 14.3 — append exclusive New York County (state and federal) venue, leaving the choice-of-law sentence intact.
8. § 3.2 — fix renewal terms at 12 months, shorten our non-renewal notice to 30 days, add a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and cap uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
9. § 3.5 — insert the playbook transition assistance and Content return/export and deletion-certification obligations (§ 3.5 already survives termination under § 14.2, so no survival amendment is needed).
10. § 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — add a 90-day conformance warranty, a no-malicious-code warranty and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and carve the § 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.
11. New § 14.12A — vendor insurance covenant at preferred levels (CGL $1M/$2M, E&O $2M, cyber $5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request). **Fallback offered:** E&O $1M / cyber $2M.

**No action required (preserve current drafting):** EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, AUDIT and NOSOLICIT. We are not proposing edits on the two "needs review" items — inserting audit or non-solicit machinery would require first drafting a restriction against ourselves, which is worse than the status quo.

**Diligence to complete before signature:**
- **Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and each Order Form are not part of the reviewed text.** We must review them for (i) early termination charges quantifying the § 3.4 exposure, (ii) committed volumes or minimum purchase obligations, (iii) any hiring restriction (we would then negotiate to the mutual 12-month fallback limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire), and (iv) initial term length, given the § 3.2 renewal mechanic.
- If a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification, apply the AUDIT parameters at that point.
- Raise a vendor-granted MFN as a commercial ask in negotiation (upside, not a deviation).
"}

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not sign as drafted:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services.** Indemnifying IBM against any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is expressly a walk-away item under the playbook, only partly mitigated by the relief in § 8.2(c). We require this narrowed to our breach of law or of this Agreement.
2. **§ 9.1(2) — blanket exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data.** In a hosting deal this removes our principal remedy and must be deleted; it also needs to be read with the absence of any data-breach indemnity in § 8.1.
3. **§ 5.4(c) — all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out.** Combined with the absence of any conformance, malicious code or remedy provision, this sits close to the walk-away position on warranties. At minimum the § 5.1 warranties must be carved out of the disclaimer.
4. **No vendor insurance where IBM processes personal data.** The playbook treats a vendor processing personal data with no insurance as a walk-away; we require the covenant at § 14.12A.
5. **§ 3.2 — automatic multi-year renewals.** Where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term, § 3.2 produces automatic multi-year renewals, which is at the walk-away boundary. Renewal terms must be fixed at 12 months.
